source_text.body:
Use voice notes, research and GitHub monitoring with an agent
A commenter uses OpenClaw for voice notes while driving, deep research on specific items, and monitoring GitHub projects for bugs and activity.
·
Jul 14, 2026
Done with
OC
OpenClaw
What they did
One commenter ran OpenClaw on a Samsung S10 FE through Termux, with Groq Whisper for speech-to-text and ElevenLabs for text-to-speech, so they could send voice notes while driving and get spoken replies back. Another used OpenClaw on a Raspberry Pi 5 for occasional deep research and GitHub monitoring, alongside workflows where it checked external sources on a schedule, tracked prior notifications in a local SQLite database, scored results, and emailed links.
How it went
The phone setup handled everyday tasks like briefings, mail summaries, appointment booking, and invoices. The Raspberry Pi user says it helped them land a very good job, but they only described the mechanics in detail for job-search workflows, not for the research or GitHub-monitoring pieces.
Worth knowing
The clearest practical catch is that the mobile voice setup relied on free tiers for Groq Whisper and ElevenLabs, while the other user ran theirs on a spare Raspberry Pi 5.
Try it yourself
with
OpenClaw
Copy prompt
Set me up with three things via [Telegram]. First, when I send a voice note, transcribe it and file it as [tasks, notes, or reminders] with any deadlines pulled out. Second, when I send you a topic, do deep research and return a sourced summary of [length]. Third, monitor these GitHub repos: [owner/repo list], and send me a daily digest of new bugs, notable issues, and activity. Don't post comments or open issues on GitHub without showing me the text first.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/openclaw/comments/1usnren/where_is_openclaw_heading_curious_how_people_are
